published_statement: Section 7 (Discussion), verbatim: 'In arriving at this conclusion it is crucial to note that we have defined flare-out in terms of the expansion properties of light rays at the throat and not in terms of "shape" functions or embedding diagrams. While the latter can certainly be used without risk for detecting flare-out in static wormholes, they are at best misleading if applied to dynamic wormholes. This is simply because the embedding of a wormhole spacetime requires selecting and lifting out a particular time-slice and embedding this instantaneous spatial three-geometry in a flat Euclidean R^3. For a static wormhole, any constant time-slice will suffice, and if the embedded surface is flared-out in the spatial direction orthogonal to the throat, then it is flared-out in spacetime as well. But if the wormhole is dynamic, flare-out in the spatial direction does not imply flare-out in the null directions orthogonal to the throat.' Section 4, verbatim: 'in the time-dependent case, it may not be possible to locate the entire throat within one time slice, as the dynamic throat is an extended object in spacetime, and the variational principle must be carried out employing surface deformations in the two independent null directions orthogonal to the hypersurface: say, delta u_+ and delta u_-. This, by the way, suggests why it is that the embedding of the spatial part of a wormhole spacetime in an Euclidean R^3 is no longer a reliable operational technique for defining "flare-out" in the time-dependent case.' The definitions it rests on (section 4.1, eqs 32-34, Table 1): a throat is a closed spatial 2-surface with theta = 0 (extremal, eq 32: theta = (1/2) gamma^{ab} d gamma_ab / du) and d theta/du >= 0 (simple flare-out, eq 34, from delta^2 A >= 0, eq 33); strong flare-out adds d theta/du > 0 at some point; a dynamic wormhole generically has two non-coincident throats (eq 42), which coalesce in the static limit (section 4.2, eqs 43-48). NEC theorem (section 5.1, eqs 49-50): at any simply flared throat, T_ab l^a l^b <= 0 -- 'violated, or on the verge of being violated'. Worked example (section 6.1, conformally scaled Morris-Thorne, eq 69): theta_+- (eq 72), d theta/du (eq 73), on theta=0 (eq 75), Einstein tensor (eq 76), and the sign-lock (rho - tau) >= 0 <=> d theta/du|_{r*} <= 0 (eq 77); static limit (eq 83). The paper's own logical form: the section-7 sentence is a non-implication stated in the Discussion; it is not a numbered theorem, and its proof is by the section-4 variational argument ('suggests') plus the section-6.1 example in which the null-extremal sphere r*(t) is not the spatial centre r0 and eq (75) is sign-indefinite.
published_hypotheses: Lorentzian spacetime with a closed spatial 2-surface and its two future-directed orthogonal null geodesic congruences l_+-; expansions theta_+- as in eq (32) (Lie derivative of the induced 2-metric along the null direction).

NO symmetry assumed ('We make no assumptions about symmetries, spherical or otherwise'), no asymptotic flatness, no null infinities, no global hyperbolicity, no embedding, no topology, no time-independence (section 1, abstract).

Flare-out is DEFINED by the null expansion and its derivative along the same null direction: theta = 0 and d theta/du >= 0 (simple), > 0 somewhere (strong); Taylor expandability of theta in u near the throat (eq 38), with an N-fold degenerate extension (eqs 39-41) when the first derivative vanishes.

For the NEC theorem (section 5.1): Einstein equation, zero torsion, twist-free congruence (hypersurface-orthogonal), sigma^2 >= 0; conclusion T_ab l^a l^b <= 0 at a simply flared throat -- equality allowed.

For the section-7 sentence specifically: 'static' means a block-diagonal metric with a timelike V^a = e^phi d_t orthogonal to constant-time slices, phi spatial only (eq 43); 'dynamic' is the negation. The spatial-flare-out side is the Morris-Thorne embedding criterion on a constant-t slice.
For the worked example (section 6.1): spherical symmetry, metric ds^2 = Omega(t)^2[-dt^2 + dr^2/(1-b/r) + r^2 dOmega^2], b(r0)=r0, two coordinate patches, Omega non-singular.

DROPPED HYPOTHESIS at driven.py:517-518 (standard_table row 'therefore the corridor needs no negative energy' = REFUTED, 'Hochberg & Visser 1998; Olum 1998') and driven.py:893-895: what gr-qc/9802046 proves is T_ab l^a l^b <= 0 AT A THROAT IN ITS SENSE -- a marginally anti-trapped surface, theta=0 with d theta/du >= 0 along the same null direction. The hypothesis 'the corridor possesses such a null-flared throat' is not stated in the row. It matters: Maeda-Harada-Carr 0901.1153 eq (4.53) with a = t/t0, t0 <= b, is a dynamic spacetime connecting two Friedmann universes through a constant-t spatial minimal sphere (x=0, flared on every slice), trapped everywhere (no marginal sphere anywhere, so no Hochberg-Visser throat exists), with the DOMINANT energy condition satisfied everywhere -- re-derived in the script (checks 'MHC ...'). gr-qc/9802046 is not contradicted by it (its theorem is silent where no anti-trapped surface exists) and the section-7 statement is confirmed by it in the strongest form (spatial flare-out for all time, null flare-out nowhere). But 'a dynamic corridor with spatial flare-out needs negative energy' does NOT follow from gr-qc/9802046 alone. In the tree the row is co-cited with Olum gr-qc/9805003, and driven.py:474/:297-298 state that LOOPHOLE_IS_EMPTY rests on nonstatic.py's kinematics with H&V as corroboration, so the dropped hypothesis is not load-bearing as the tree stands. Recorded, not repaired.

rederivation.outcome: 35 PASS, 0 FAIL, 1 DISCREPANCY recorded; exit 0; ~7 s (sympy 1.14.0, python 3.11). Verified from Christoffel symbols of the paper's metric (69): eq (72) theta_+- exactly as printed and equal to (2/R) l(R); eq (73) d theta/du exactly; eq (75) from (73)+(74); eq (76) G_tt+G_rr (orthonormal) exactly; eq (77) as the identity 8 pi (rho - tau) = -2 d theta/du on the extremal sphere (sign-locked, so 'suspend the NEC violation <=> destroy the flare-out' is an identity, not an inequality); static limit theta=0 <=> b=r (eqs 74/83). DISCREPANCY: printed eq (83) gives (1 - b'(r0))/r0^2, but the static limit of the paper's own (73)/(75) is (1 - b'(r0))/(2 r0^2) -- a factor 2, positive, sign unchanged, no consequence in the paper or the tree; a misprint or an unstated renormalisation of l, recorded and not quoted as an error. foliation.py:243's theta_+ = (2/R)(U + Gamma) verified for the general diagonal spherically symmetric metric, with the zero set and sign(d theta/du) on theta=0 shown normalisation-independent (Maeda-Harada-Carr eq 2.10). INSTANCE 1 (the section-7 statement shown, not asserted): b = r0^2/r, Omega = e^{-t/3}: the constant-t centre r0=1 is Morris-Thorne flared-out at all t, theta_+ != 0 there, and of the two null-extremal spheres r* = 1.0705 (flared, +) and r* = 2.8025 (NOT flared, -) -- spatial flare-out at the centre implies null flare-out at no surface in general. INSTANCE 2 (Maeda-Harada-Carr 0901.1153 eqs 4.53-4.61 re-derived): a = t/t0, t0 < 2b: x=0 is a spatial minimal sphere with flare-out on every slice, theta_+ theta_- > 0 everywhere (no anti-trapped surface, no H&V throat), and mu + p_r = (2/t^2)[1 - t0^2 b^2/(x^2+b^2)^2] >= 0 everywhere iff t0 <= b (NEC, indeed DEC, holds).

later_literature.ref: S. A. Hayward, 'Dynamic wormholes', gr-qc/9805019, Int. J. Mod. Phys. D8, 373 (1999)
later_literature.what: Defines a wormhole horizon as a TEMPORAL OUTER trapping horizon (derivative along the OTHER null direction, strict inequality). States that H&V's strict flare-out 'is implied by the above definition. However, the converse is not so, since Hochberg & Visser specifically allow spatial horizons, in which case their flare-out condition selects maximal rather than minimal surfaces in a time-symmetric hypersurface.' Agrees on the substance the tree uses: the static definition is 'a minimal surface in a static spatial hypersurface'; dynamically 'the spatial surface is minimal in SOME spatial hypersurface' and is then generically a trapped surface -- so the constant-t criterion is slice-dependent. NEC violated everywhere on a generic (strict) wormhole horizon; non-strict flare-out lets 'negative energy just barely be avoided in very special cases'.

later_literature.ref: S. A. Hayward, 'Wormhole dynamics in spherical symmetry', arXiv:0903.5438, Phys. Rev. D 79, 124001 (2009)
later_literature.what: Same comparison in detail (sec III): H&V use 'a non-strict version of (31) rather than kappa > 0. However, they specifically allowed spatial xi, which does not give local two-way traversability and for which (31) can select maximal rather than minimal surfaces' (Robertson-Walker bounce counterexample). Sec IV: 'it is not recommended to generalize by naively inserting time-dependent ... factors into a metric which is singular precisely at the object of interest' -- the same warning as H&V section 7 in Hayward's words. Sec V: 'Claims that this need not be so in Einstein gravity either do not involve traversable wormholes as defined here, or evaluate energy density somewhere other than a mouth, e.g. at a centre of symmetry described as a "throat"' -- which is exactly the spatial-centre-vs-null-throat distinction of H&V section 6.1.4.

later_literature.ref: H. Maeda, T. Harada, B. J. Carr, 'Cosmological wormholes', arXiv:0901.1153, Phys. Rev. D 79, 044034 (2009)
later_literature.what: Sec III.B: in spherical symmetry the H&V throat is theta_+ = 0, d_+ theta_+ > 0; a Hayward throat is necessarily an H&V throat, not conversely (the H&V throat may be spacelike); NEC violated at both (eq 3.8). Sec III.C-IV: defines a throat on a SPACELIKE hypersurface instead, shows it is a trapped sphere or a bifurcating horizon, and exhibits cosmological wormholes (eq 4.53, a=t/t0, t0 <= b) that connect two Friedmann universes, are trapped everywhere with NO trapping horizon (so are 'not Hochberg-Visser or Hayward wormholes'), and satisfy the dominant energy condition everywhere. Also states 'any definition in terms of time-slicing will inevitably entail the problem of slice-dependence'. Effect on the audited statement: CONFIRMS it in the strongest form (spatial flare-out on every slice, null flare-out nowhere). Effect on the tree's driven.py:517 row: shows that H&V's NEC theorem alone does not reach a spatially-flared dynamic corridor without a null throat. Their eqs 4.54-4.57, 4.61 re-derived in the script.

later_literature.ref: Y. Tomikawa, K. Izumi, T. Shiromizu, 'New definition of wormhole throat', arXiv:1503.01926 (2015)
later_literature.what: Proposes k = theta_+ - theta_- = 0 with r^a nabla_a k > 0 on a quasi-local slice, as a hybrid of the null (H&V, Hayward) and spacelike (Maeda et al.) definitions, because the spacelike one 'strongly depends on which spacelike hypersurfaces we take ... even de Sitter and FLRW spacetimes are categorized into wormhole'. Sec II eq (15): with the NEC, r^a nabla_a k + t^a nabla_a kbar <= 0, so 'for a sort of static case' flare-out fails under the NEC ('a simple confirmation of well-known fact'); in the dynamical Ellis case (sec III.B.5) a DEC-respecting throat exists 'in a certain time interval of the universe and the size is about the Hubble radius' -- 'it seems hard or impossible to construct [small] wormholes without violating the energy condition'. Confirms slice-dependence of any constant-t criterion; does not contradict H&V section 7.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis -- that earlier physicists 'may have all lacked certain data' -- has no purchase on this result: it is a piece of Lorentzian differential geometry whose every input is a definition (expansion of a null congruence, area variation) and two identities (Raychaudhuri, Einstein). No measurement of any kind enters, and none has arrived since 1998 that could. What the authors DID lack in 1998 was not data but the later definitional literature: Hayward's temporal-outer-trapping-horizon definition (1999, 2009), Maeda-Harada-Carr's spacelike-slice definition and their DEC-respecting cosmological wormholes (2009), and Tomikawa-Izumi-Shiromizu's hybrid (2015). Evidence either way: (a) FOR 'incomplete': the H&V definition admits spacelike throats where its flare-out picks maximal surfaces (Hayward's Robertson-Walker bounce), so 'throat' in their sense is broader than a traversable mouth; and their NEC theorem is silent on spatially-flared dynamic corridors with no anti-trapped surface, which exist with the DEC satisfied (MHC eq 4.53, re-derived here). (b) AGAINST 'wrong': every later paper read confirms the audited sentence -- the constant-t/embedding criterion is slice-dependent and says nothing about null flare-out once staticity goes -- and none of it moves a single equation of the paper; the one algebraic discrepancy found (eq 83, factor 2) is positive and changes no sign. Net: having the later literature narrows the NEC corollary's reach, and leaves the section-7 statement exactly where it was.
grade_evidence: (1) The statement as the tree uses it -- foliation.py:243-248 D5, :384-385, :615-616, :876; driven.py:84-92, :297-298, :311-312, :893 -- is the source's section-7 sentence verbatim (driven.py:84-86) and the section-4 sentence near-verbatim. (2) Hypotheses: the tree uses it on spherical symmetry, a subclass of the source's no-symmetry class; nothing the source requires is dropped for the section-7 statement itself. (3) Re-derivation agrees: eqs 72, 73, 75, 76, 77 and the static limit re-derived from Christoffels of the paper's metric, 35/35 checks pass; the non-implication is SHOWN by two explicit instances (Ellis b=r0^2/r with Omega=e^{-t/3}: spatial flare-out at the centre, one null-extremal sphere flared and one not; MHC a=t/t0: spatial flare-out on every slice, no null throat anywhere), so it is theorem-strength even though the source states it in a Discussion. (4) No datum: none enters. (5) Later literature (Hayward 1999/2009, Maeda-Harada-Carr 2009, Tomikawa et al. 2015) confirms it uniformly and narrows only the NEC corollary's class. (6) The single discrepancy found -- printed eq (83) is 2x the static limit of the paper's own (73)/(75) -- is a positive factor with no sign or conclusion attached, and is recorded per the fluctuation.py precedent, not quoted as an error. (7) The one dropped hypothesis in the tree (driven.py:517-518: the NEC corollary needs an H&V throat, and the row does not say so) attaches to a different claim of the same paper, is co-cited with Olum, and the tree states elsewhere (driven.py:297-298, :474) that H&V is corroboration rather than ground -- so it is recorded as drift, not as a narrowing of the audited result.
what_would_change_the_grade: To NARROWED: if driven.py:517-518's REFUTED row were read as resting on gr-qc/9802046 alone (Olum gr-qc/9805003 removed or itself graded down), because H&V's NEC theorem carries the hypothesis 'a marginally anti-trapped surface exists' and Maeda-Harada-Carr's eq (4.53) with t0 <= b is a re-derived, DEC-satisfying dynamic corridor with spatial flare-out on every slice and no such surface. To WRONG: a dynamic spacetime in which every constant-t spatially flared-out throat is also a null-flared throat -- i.e. a proof that the implication holds off staticity -- which instance 1 and instance 2 of the script already exclude in the spherically symmetric conformal-Morris-Thorne and cosmological-Ellis classes. To OPEN: nothing; the source was read at source and every closed-form equation used was re-derived.
